arxiv-2301-02896.creator: Devvrat Joshi, Janvi Thakkar
arxiv-2301-02896.description: Abstract In today’s data-driven world, the sensitivity of information has been a significant concern. With this data and additional information on the person’s background, one can easily infer an individual’s private data. Many differentially private iterative algorithms have been proposed in interactive settings to protect an individual’s privacy from these inference attacks.

arxiv-2310-10026.creator: Kashyap Patel 1 , Anton Kovalyov, and Issa Panahi
arxiv-2310-10026.description: Abstract This paper introduces a practical approach for leveraging a real-time deep learning model to alternate between speech enhancement and joint speech enhancement and separation depending on whether the input mixture contains one or two active speakers. Scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio (SI-SDR) has shown to be a highly effective training measure in time-domain speech separation.

arxiv-2311-05542.title: Counterexamples to conjectures on the occupancy fraction of graphs
arxiv-2311-05542.creator: Stijn Cambie, Jorik Jooken
arxiv-2311-05542.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Stijn Cambie, Jorik Jooken. The occupancy fraction of a graph is a (normalized) measure on the size of independent sets under the hard-core model, depending on a variable (fugacity) λ . We present a criterion for finding the graph with minimum occupancy fraction among graphs with a fixed order, and disprove five conjectures on the extremes of the occupancy fraction and (normalized) independence polynomial for certain graph classes of regular graphs with a given girth.

arxiv-2405-09915.title: Sparse Regression Codes for Non-coherent SIMO channels This work is supported in part by the Qualcomm 6G UR grant and partly by the Prime Minister’s Research Fund (PMRF). The authors are with the Department of Electrical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Madras, Chennai - 600036, Tamil Nad
arxiv-2405-09915.creator: Sai Dinesh Kancharana, Madhusudan Kumar Sinha, Arun Pachai Kannu
arxiv-2405-09915.description: Abstract Motivated by hyper-reliable low-latency communication in 6G, we consider error control coding for short block lengths in multi-antenna fading channels. In general, the channel fading coefficients are unknown at both the transmitter and receiver, which is referred to as non-coherent channels. Conventionally, pilot symbols are transmitted to facilitate channel estimation, causing power and bandwidth overhead.

arxiv-2411-07895.title: Homological stability for symplectic groups via algebraic arc complexes
arxiv-2411-07895.creator: Ismael Sierra, Nathalie Wahl
arxiv-2411-07895.description: Abstract . We use algebraic arc complexes to prove a homological stability result for symplectic groups with slope 2 3 \frac{2}{3} for rings with finite unitary stable rank. Symplectic groups are here interpreted as the automorphism groups of formed spaces with boundary , which are algebraic analogues of surfaces with boundary, that we also study in the present paper.

arxiv-2412-04729.title: Espresso : High Compression For Rich Extraction From Videos for Your Vision-Language Model
arxiv-2412-04729.creator: Keunwoo Peter Yu, Achal Dave, Rare s , Ambru s ,, Jean Mercat
arxiv-2412-04729.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Keunwoo Peter Yu, Achal Dave, Rare s , Ambru s ,, Jean Mercat. Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have shown great promise in connecting images and text, but extending these models to long videos remains challenging due to the rapid growth in token counts. Models that compress videos by local aggregation in time or space have become popular for handling long-form inputs; however, these pooling-based projectors sacrifice the benefits of fixed-length representations that are crucial for streaming and efficient video understanding.

arxiv-2505-21545.title: Corruption-Aware Training of Latent Video Diffusion Models for Robust Text-to-Video Generation
arxiv-2505-21545.creator: Chika Maduabuchi, Hao Chen, Yujin Han, Jindong Wang
arxiv-2505-21545.description: Abstract Latent Video Diffusion Models (LVDMs) have achieved remarkable generative quality but remain sensitive to imperfect conditioning, leading to semantic drift and temporal incoherence when trained on web-scale, noisy video-text corpora. We introduce CAT-LVDM , the first corruption-aware training framework for LVDMs, which enhances robustness through structured, data-aligned noise injection.

arxiv-2507-16181.title: Pulse-Level Simulation of Crosstalk Attacks on Superconducting Quantum Hardware †
arxiv-2507-16181.creator: Syed Emad Uddin Shubha, Tasnuva Farheen
arxiv-2507-16181.description: Abstract Hardware crosstalk in multi-tenant superconducting quantum computers poses a severe security threat, allowing adversaries to induce targeted errors across tenant boundaries by injecting carefully engineered pulses. We present a simulation-based study of active crosstalk attacks at the pulse level, analyzing how adversarial control of pulse timing, shape, amplitude, and coupling can disrupt a victim’s computation.

pmc-10519563.description: Summary:This practical review critically evaluates the evidence behind the widespread use of postoperative compression therapy intended to improve surgical outcomes, such as reduced edema, ecchymosis, pain, and seroma formation. pmc-10712119.description: BackgroundCeliac disease (CeD) is an immune-mediated disorder that develops in genetically predisposed individuals upon gluten consumption. HLA risk alleles explain 40% of the genetic component of CeD, so there have been continuing efforts to uncover non-HLA loci that can explain the remaining heritability. As in most autoimmune disorders, the prevalence of CeD is significantly higher in women.

pmc-11757104.creator: Sungun Bang, Young Jin Ahn, Kyo Chul Koo
pmc-11757104.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The prediction of survival outcomes is a key factor in making decisions for prostate cancer (PCa) treatment. Advances in computer-based technologies have increased the role of machine learning (ML) methods in predicting cancer prognosis. Due to the various effective treatments available for each non-linear landscape of PCa, the integration of ML can help offer tailored treatment strategies and precision medicine approaches, thus improving survival in patients with PCa.

pmc-13037149.title: 2H-pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidin-4-amine derivatives as novel selective fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) inhibitors
pmc-13037149.creator: Pinglian Wu, Zhaodi Tian, Weizhong Shen, Qiuju Xun, Yuan Tian, Huiqiong Li, Bowen Yang, Shaohua Chang, Weixue Huang, Zhen Wang, Ke Ding, Dawei Ma
pmc-13037149.description: Although FGFR2 is a well-validated oncogenic target, no selective FGFR2 inhibitors have been approved for clinical use. In this study, we report the discovery of 2H-pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidin-4-amine derivative as novel, irreversible FGFR2 inhibitors. The optimal compound, PLW559, potently inhibited FGFR2 with an IC50 value of 13.59 nM and demonstrated exceptional selectivity over FGFR1, FGFR3, and FGFR4.

pmc-13589969.title: Correlation of Mitochondrial Flavoprotein Fluorescence and Sectoral OCT in Patients with Glaucoma, Suspects, and Ocular Hypertension
pmc-13589969.creator: Tiffany Heaster-Ford, Rafaella Nascimento e Silva, Justin Elstrott, Dolly S Chang, Julia A Kim, Joyce Kang, Yan Zhao, Yihao Li, Chen Chen, Sofia De Arrigunaga, Sandra E Freeman, Kanza Aziz, Collin A Rich, Michael M Lin, David S Friedman
pmc-13589969.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeFlavoprotein fluorescence (FPF) can be measured using a noninvasive investigational device, the OcuMet Beacon (OcuSciences). The Beacon uses blue light to stimulate oxidized mitochondrial flavoproteins, which subsequently emit green autofluorescence. As mitochondrial metabolic stress may reflect axonal damage in glaucomatous eyes, this cross-sectional, exploratory study investigated relationships between optical coherence tomography (OCT) structural parameters and FPF values in patients with glaucoma, ocular hypertension, and glaucoma suspects.Patients and MethodsIndividuals with mild/moderate glaucoma, suspected glaucoma, or ocular hypertension receiving treatment.

pmc-13677266.title: Dynamics of ventriculo-arterial coupling and peripheral tissue perfusion during early resuscitation of septic shock
pmc-13677266.creator: Juan Daniel Caicedo Ruiz, Gustavo García Gallardo, Jose Luis Aldana, Eduardo Kattan, Ricardo Castro, Glenn Hernandez, Michael Pinsky, Jihad Mallat, Gustavo Adolfo Ospina-Tascón
pmc-13677266.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Graphical abstractKeywords: Arterial elastance, Capillary refill time, End-systolic left-ventricle elastance, Peripheral perfusion, Septic shock, Ventriculo-arterial coupling

Introduction

Resuscitation of septic shock relies on the assumption that optimizing macrohemodynamics will reverse tissue hypoxia and the metabolic derangements of shock [1]. However, cardiovascular dysfunction in septic shock results from a variable combination of pathological vasodilation, relative or absolute hypovolemia, microvascular flow misdistribution, and cardiac dysfunction [2,3], implying that resuscitation should be individually adjusted.
